questions.question: The total surface area of a solid hemisphere is 1039.5 cm 2 . The volume (in cm 3 ) of the hemisphere is: (Take π = 22/7)
questions.questionHtml: The total surface area of a solid hemisphere is 1039.5 cm<sup>2</sup>. The volume (in cm<sup>3</sup>) of the hemisphere is: (Take π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
Given:

TSA of hemisphere = 1039.5 cm2

Formula used:

Total surface area of the hemisphere = 3πr2

Volume of the hemisphere = (2/3) × πr3

Calculation:

⇒ 3πr2 = 1039.5

⇒ 3 × (22/7) × r2 = 1039.5

⇒ r2 = (1039.5 × 7)/(3 × 22) = 15.75 × 7 = 2.25 × 7 × 7

⇒ r = 1.5 × 7 = 10.5

Volume of the hemisphere = (2/3) × π r3 = (2/3) × (22/7) × 10.5 × 10.5 × `10.5 = 2425.5

∴ The correct answer is 2425.5

questions.question: The total surface area of a solid metallic hemisphere is 462 cm 2 . This is melted and moulded into a right circular cone. If the radius of the base of the cone is the same as that of the hemisphere, then its height is: (use π = 22/7)
questions.questionHtml: The total surface area of a solid metallic hemisphere is 462 cm<sup>2</sup>. This is melted and moulded into a right circular cone. If the radius of the base of the cone is the same as that of the hemisphere, then its height is: (use π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
Given:

The total surface area of a solid metallic hemisphere is 462 cm2.

Hemisphere is melted into a right circular cone

The radius of the base of the cone is the same as that of the hemisphere

Formula Used:

The Surface area of the Hemisphere = \(3\pi r^2\)

The volume of the hemisphere = \(\frac{2}{3}\pi r^3\)

The volume of cone=\(\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2h\)

Calculations:

⇒ The Surface area of the Hemisphere = \(3\pi r^2\)

⇒ \(462=3\times \frac{22}{7}\times r^2\)

⇒ r2 = 7 x 7

⇒ r = 7 cm

⇒ The radius of the cone = 7 cm

As Hemisphere is melted into a right circular cone, then

⇒ The volume of the Hemisphere = Volume of a cone

⇒ \(\frac{2}{3}\pi r^3= \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2h\)

⇒ \(2r = h\)

⇒ h = 2 x 7 = 14 cm

⇒ Hence, The height of the cone is 14 cm.

questions.question: A cuboidal water purifier can carry 10 litres of water. Its breadth is \(\frac{1}{5}\) of its height and length is \(\frac{1}{3}\) of the sum of the breadth and height. The height of the tank is:
questions.questionHtml: A cuboidal water purifier can carry 10 litres of water. Its breadth is \(\frac{1}{5}\) of its height and length is \(\frac{1}{3}\) of the sum of the breadth and height. The height of the tank is:
questions.solution:
Given:

A cuboidal water purifier can carry 10 litres of water. Its breadth is (1)/(5) of its height and length is (1)/(3) of the sum of the breadth and height.

Formula used:

Volume of cuboid = length × breadth × height

1 litre = 1000 cm3

Calculations:

Volume = 10 litres = 10 × 1000 cm3 = 10000 cm3

Let height = h cm

Breadth = (1/5)h cm

Length = (1/3)(h + (1/5)h) cm

⇒ Length = (1/3)(6h/5) cm

⇒ Length = 2h/5 cm

Volume = length × breadth × height

⇒ 10000 = (2h/5) × (h/5) × h

⇒ 10000 = (2h3)/(25)

⇒ 10000 × 25 = 2h3

⇒ 250000 = 2h3

⇒ h3 = 125000

⇒ h = ∛125000

⇒ h = 50 cm

∴ The correct answer is option 3.

questions.question: A 9 cm solid metallic cube and a solid metallic cuboid having dimensions 5 cm, 13 cm, 31 cm are melted and recast into a single cube. What is the total surface area (in cm 2 ) of the new cube?
questions.questionHtml: A 9 cm solid metallic cube and a solid metallic cuboid having dimensions 5 cm, 13 cm, 31 cm are melted and recast into a single cube. What is the total surface area (in cm<sup>2</sup>) of the new cube?
questions.solution:
Given:

Side of cube = 9 cm

Cuboid Dimensions

Length = 5 cm, breadth = 13 cm, height = 31 cm

Formula used:

Volume of cube = (side)3

Volume of cuboid = length × breadth × height

Total surface area of cube = 6 × side2

Calculation:

Volume of Solid metallic cube

⇒ 93

⇒ 729 cm3

Volume of Solid metallic cuboid

⇒ 5 × 13 × 31

⇒ 2015 cm3

Volume of Recast single cube

⇒ Volume of Solid metallic cube + Volume of Solid metallic cuboid

⇒ 729 + 2015

⇒ 2744 cm3

Side of Recast cube

⇒ (Side)3 = 2744

⇒ side = 14 cm

Total surface area of cube

⇒ 6 × 14 × 14

⇒ 1176 cm2

∴ The total surface area of recast cube is 1176 cm2.

questions.question: Find the volume (in cm 3 ) of a hemisphere of radius 18 cm. (Use \(\pi=\frac{22}{7}\) ) (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.questionHtml: Find the volume (in cm3) of a hemisphere of radius 18 cm. (Use \(\pi=\frac{22}{7}\)) (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.solution:
Given:

Radius (r) = 18 cm

Formula used:

Volume of hemisphere = \(\dfrac{2}{3} \pi r^3\)

Where, \(\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}\)

Calculations:

Volume = \(\dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 18^3\)

⇒ Volume = \(\dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 18 \times 18 \times 18\)

⇒ Volume = \(\dfrac{2 \times 22 \times 5832}{3 \times 7}\)

⇒ Volume = \(\dfrac{256608}{21}\)

⇒ Volume ≈ 12219.43 cm3

∴ The correct answer is option (2).

questions.questionHtml: Some ice pieces, spherical in shape, of diameter 6 cm are dropped in a cylindrical container containing some juice and are fully submerged. If the diameter of the container is 18 cm and level of juice rises by 40 cm, then how many ice pieces are dropped in the container?

Radius of sphere = 6/2 = 3 cm

Radius of cylinder = 18/2 = 9 cm 

Number of spherical ice pieces dropped in cylinder is,

x = (Volume of cylinder) / (Volume of sphere)

x = \(\frac{\pi\times 9^2\times40}{\frac{4}{3}\times\pi\times3^3}\)⇒ 90 [take height of cyclinder, h = 40 cm]

questions.question: The ratio of the slant height and the height of a cone is 4 : 3. If the curved surface area of the cone is \(4 \sqrt{7} \pi\) square units, then the radius of the cone is _________ units.
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of the slant height and the height of a cone is 4 : 3. If the curved surface area of the cone is \(4 \sqrt{7} \pi\) square units, then the radius of the cone is _________ units.
questions.solution:
Given:

The ratio of the slant height and the height of a cone is 4 : 3.

Curved surface area of the cone is 4√7π square units.

Formula used:

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a cone = πrl

Where, r = radius, l = slant height

Calculations:

Ratio of slant height to height = 4:3

⇒ l/h = 4/3

⇒ l = 4k and h = 3k (assuming k is a constant)

⇒ By Pythagoras theorem in the right triangle formed by the radius, height, and slant height:

l2 = r2 + h2

⇒ (4k)2 = r2 + (3k)2

⇒ 16k2 = r2 + 9k2

⇒ r2 = 16k2 - 9k2

⇒ r2 = 7k2

⇒ r = √(7k2)

⇒ r = k√7

Curved Surface Area = 4√7π

⇒ πrl = 4√7π

⇒ r × l = 4√7

⇒ k√7 × 4k = 4√7

⇒ 4k2√7 = 4√7

⇒ k2 = 1

⇒ k = 1

⇒ r = 1×√7

⇒ r = √7

∴ The correct answer is option (4).

questions.question: A solid metallic cube of side 9 cm and a solid metallic cuboid having dimensions 5 cm, 13 cm, 31 cm are melted to from a single cube. How much (in Rs.) is the cost to polish the new cube at a rate of Rs. 10 per cm 2 ?
questions.questionHtml: A solid metallic cube of side 9 cm and a solid metallic cuboid having dimensions 5 cm, 13 cm, 31 cm are melted to from a single cube. How much (in Rs.) is the cost to polish the new cube at a rate of Rs. 10 per cm<sup>2</sup>?
questions.solution:
Given:

Dimensions of a solid metallic cube = 9 cm

Dimensions of a solid metallic cuboid = 5 cm, 13 cm, 31 cm

Rate of Polishing a new cube = Rs. 10 per cm2

Formula Used:

Total Surface area of a cube = 6(side)2

Volume of cube = (side)3

Volume of cuboid = (length × breadth × height)

Amount to polish the cube = Rate × Total surface area of cube

Calculation:

Volume of the new cube = Volume of solid metallic cube + Volume of solid metallic cuboid

Volume of solid metallic cube = (9 cm)3 = 729 cm3

Volume of solid metallic cuboid = (5 cm × 13 cm × 31 cm) = 2015 cm3

⇒ Volume of the new cube = (729 cm3 + 2015 cm3) = 2744 cm3 

⇒ (side)3 = 2744 cm3 

⇒ side of new cube = 14 cm  

Total surface area of the new cube = 6(14 cm)2 = 6 × 196 cm2 = 1176 cm2

Amount to polish the cube = Rs. 10 per cm2 × 1176 cm2 = Rs. 11,760

∴ Cost to polish the new cube is Rs. 11,760

questions.question: The curved surface area of a right circular cylinder of height 56 cm is 1408 cm 2 . Find the diameter of the base of the cylinder.
questions.questionHtml: The curved surface area of a right circular cylinder of height 56 cm is 1408 cm<sup>2</sup>. Find the diameter of the base of the cylinder.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Direct formula for Curved Surface Area (CSA) using Diameter (d): π × d × h = 1408

(22/7) × d × 56 = 1408

22 × d × 8 = 1408

176 × d = 1408

d = 1408 ÷ 176 = 8 cm = 0.08 m

∴ The correct answer is 0.08 m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Height (h) of the cylinder = 56 cm

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 1408 cm2

Formula Used:

Curved Surface Area of a right circular cylinder = 2 × π × r × h

Where r is the radius and h is the height.

Calculations:

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r × 56 = 1408

⇒ 44 × r × (56 ÷ 7) = 1408

⇒ 44 × r × 8 = 1408

⇒ 352 × r = 1408

⇒ r = 1408 ÷ 352

⇒ r = 4 cm

⇒ Diameter (d) = 2 × r = 2 × 4 = 8 cm

⇒ In meters: d = 8 ÷ 100 m = 0.08 m

∴ The correct answer is 0.08 m.

Additional Information

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Cylinder

The total surface area includes the curved surface and the areas of the two circular bases: TSA = 2 × π × r × (h + r).

Volume of Cylinder

The space occupied by the cylinder is given by the formula: Volume = π × r2 × h.

Metric Conversion

To convert centimeters to meters, divide the value by 100 (1 m = 100 cm).

questions.question: The radius of a sphere is increased by 25%. What is the increase per cent in surface area?
questions.questionHtml: The radius of a sphere is increased by 25%. What is the increase per cent in surface area?
questions.solution:
Initial radius = r, New radius = 1.25r

Initial surface area = 4πr2, New surface area = 4π(1.25r)2 ⇒  4π(1.5625r2) = 6.25πr2

Increase = 6.25πr2 - 4πr2 = 2.25πr2

Percentage increase = (2.25πr2/4πr2) × 100 = 0.5625 × 100 = 56.25%

questions.question: The ratio of the heights of a right circular cone and a right circular cylinder is 8 : 9 and the ratio of the radii of their bases is 3 : 4. If the volume of the cylinder is 132 cm 3 , then the volume (in cm 3 ) of the cone is:
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of the heights of a right circular cone and a right circular cylinder is 8 : 9 and the ratio of the radii of their bases is 3 : 4. If the volume of the cylinder is 132 cm<sup>3</sup> , then the volume (in cm<sup>3</sup>) of the cone is:
questions.solution:
Given :

The ratio of heights of the cone to the cylinder is 8 : 9 

The ratio of radii of the cone to the cylinder is 3 : 4 

Formula used :

The volume of a cylinder = π r2 h (where r and h are radius and height of the cylinder)

The volume of a cone = (1/3) π r2 h  (where r and h are radius and height of the cone)

Calculations :

Let the height of the cone be '8x' and the height of the cylinder be '9x' 

Let the radius of the cone be '3y' and the radius of the cylinder be '4y' 

The volume of the cylinder = π (4y)2 9x 

132 = π × 16y2 × 9x

x.y2 = 7/24 

Now volume of cone 

Volume of the cone = (1/3) π (3y)2 8x 

⇒ π 3y2 × 8x = π 24 × y2x           (putting y2x = 7/24)

⇒ 22 cm3 

∴ The volume of the cone will be 22 cm3

questions.question: A sphere passes through the eight corners of a cube of side 14 cm. Find the volume (in cm 3 ) of the sphere. Take π = 22/7
questions.questionHtml:
A sphere passes through the eight corners of a cube of side 14 cm. Find the volume (in cm3) of the sphere.

Take π = 22/7
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a sphere circumscribing a cube, its diameter is equal to the body diagonal of the cube.

Diameter = a√3 = 14√3 cm ⇒ Radius (r) = 7√3 cm.

Volume of the sphere = (4/3) × π × r3

Volume = (4/3) × (22/7) × (7√3)3 = 4312√3 cm3.

∴ The correct answer is 4312√3 cm3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Side of the cube (a) = 14 cm

Formula Used:

Diameter of a circumscribed sphere (D) = Body diagonal of the cube = a√3

Volume of a sphere = (4/3)πr3

Calculations:

⇒ Diameter of the sphere (D) = 14√3 cm

⇒ Radius of the sphere (r) = D ÷ 2 = 7√3 cm

⇒ Volume of the sphere = (4/3) × (22/7) × (7√3)3

⇒ Volume = (4/3) × (22/7) × (343 × 3√3)

⇒ Volume = 4 × 22 × 49 × √3

⇒ Volume = 88 × 49 × √3

⇒ Volume = 4312√3 cm3

∴ The correct answer is 4312√3 cm3.

Additional Information

Sphere Circumscribing a Cube

The sphere passes through all eight vertices of the cube. Its diameter is equal to the body diagonal: D = a√3.

Sphere Inscribed in a Cube

The sphere touches all six faces of the cube. Its diameter is equal to the side length of the cube: D = a.

Key Mensuration Formulas

Total Surface Area of a Cube = 6a2 | Total Surface Area of a Sphere = 4πr2.

questions.question: What is the total surface area of a cone whose radius is \(\frac{r}{4}\) and slant height is 4l ?
questions.questionHtml: What is the total surface area of a cone whose radius is \(\frac{r}{4}\) and slant height is 4l ?
questions.solution:
Given: radius = r/4, slant height = 4l


TSA of cone = πr(r + l) = π(r/4)((r/4) + 4l) = π(r/4)(r/16 + 4l) = πr(l + r/16)

questions.question: The volume of a metallic cylindrical pipe is 3564 cm 3 . If its external radius is 12 cm and thickness is 3 cm, then the length of the pipe will be: (take π = 22/7)
questions.questionHtml: The volume of a metallic cylindrical pipe is 3564 cm<sup>3</sup>. If its external radius is 12 cm and thickness is 3 cm, then the length of the pipe will be: (take π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
Given:

Volume of cylindrical pipe = 3564 cubic.cm

Formula:

Volume of cylinder = πr2h

Calculation:

Internal radius = 12 - 3 = 9 cm

Then,

⇒ 3564 = 22/7 × (122 - 92) × h

⇒ h = 18

∴ Length of pipe is 18cm

questions.question: A hemispherical bowl has a radius of 7 cm. It is to be painted from inside as well as outside. Find the cost of painting it at the rate of Rs.40 per 20 cm 2 ? (Take thickness of the bowl as negligible).
questions.questionHtml: A hemispherical bowl has a radius of 7 cm. It is to be painted from inside as well as outside. Find the cost of painting it at the rate of Rs.40 per 20 cm<sup>2</sup>? (Take thickness of the bowl as negligible).
questions.solution:
Inside Surface Area = 2π(7 cm)² = 2 × 22/7 ×  49 = 308 cm²

Outside Surface Area = 2π(7 cm)² = 308 cm²

Total Surface Area = Inside Surface Area + Outside Surface Area

Total Surface Area = 616cm² 

The cost of painting this area at the given rate of Rs. 40 for 20 cm²

Cost = (Total Surface Area / 20 cm²)   × Rs. 40

Cost = (616 / 20) × 40 = 1232 Rs.     .

questions.question: The sum of the radius of the base and the height of a cylinder is 42 m. If the total surface area of the cylinder is 6336 m 2 , find the curved surface area of the cylinder correct to two places of decimals (use π = \(\frac{22}{7}\) ).
questions.questionHtml: The sum of the radius of the base and the height of a cylinder is 42 m. If the total surface area of the cylinder is 6336 m2, find the curved surface area of the cylinder correct to two places of decimals (use π = \(\frac{22}{7}\)).

options.html: 2571.43 m2
2715.43 m2
2517.43 m2

questions.solution:
As per the question, r + h = 42

2πr (r + h) =  6336 

⇒ 2πr × 42 = 6336

⇒ r = 6336 / 264 ⇒ r = 24

Then h = 42 - 24 ⇒ 18m

Curved surface area will be , 2πrh ⇒ 2 × 22/7 × 18 × 24 = 2715.43 m2

questions.question: A drainage tile is a cylindrical shell 42 cm long. The inside and outside diameters are 8 cm and 14 cm, respectively. What is the volume (in cm 3 ) of clay required for the tile? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.questionHtml: A drainage tile is a cylindrical shell 42 cm long. The inside and outside diameters are 8 cm and 14 cm, respectively. What is the volume (in cm<sup>3</sup>) of clay required for the tile? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
Volume of outer cylinder: π × 72 × 42, 22/7 × 49 × 42 = 22 × 49 × 6 = 6,468 cm3

Volume of inner cylinder: π × 42 × 42, 22/7 × 16 × 42 = 22 × 16 × 6 = 2,112 cm3

Volume of clay required: 6,468 - 2,112 = 4,356 cm3

questions.question: A solid cone with curved surface area twice its base area has slant height of 6√3 cm. Its height is:
questions.questionHtml: A solid cone with curved surface area twice its base area has slant height of 6√3 cm. Its height is:
questions.solution:
Let the radius of the cone be r units.

⇒ πrl = 2πr2 ⇒ l = 2r ⇒ r = 6√3/2 ⇒ r = 3√3

Slant height (l) of cone = √r2 + h2 ⇒ 6√32 = 3√32 + h2 ⇒ h2 = 108 - 27 = 81 ⇒ h = 9 cm

questions.question: The ratio of the volume of first and second cylinder is 32 ∶ 9 and the ratio of their heights is 8 ∶ 9. If the area of the base of the second cylinder is 616 cm 2 , then what will be the radius of the first cylinder?
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of the volume of first and second cylinder is 32 ∶ 9 and the ratio of their heights is 8 ∶ 9. If the area of the base of the second cylinder is 616 cm2, then what will be the radius of the first cylinder?
questions.solution:
Volume of second cylinder = 616 × 9h

Let the radius of first cylinder be r, then volume of first cylinder = πr2 × 8h

Their ratios can be written as ⇒ 616 × 9h/ (πr2 × 8h) = 9/32 ⇒  (22r2 × 8)/(616 × 9 × 7)/ = 32/9 ⇒ r = 28

Volume of cuboid = 50 × 150 × 175 = 1312500 cm3

Volume of largest cube = 253 = 15625 cm3

Number of cubes = 1312500 / 15625 = 84

questions.question: A cylindrical tank of capacity 64π litres has equal height and radius. What would be the radius of the cylinder? (1 litre = 1000 cm 3 )
questions.questionHtml:
A cylindrical tank of capacity 64π litres has equal height and radius. What would be the radius of the cylinder?

(1 litre = 1000 cm3)
questions.solution:
GIVEN:

Capacity of a cylindrical tank = 64\(\pi\) 

Height of tank = Radius of tank

FORMULA USED:

Volume of the tank = \(\pi\) r2 h 

Where, r = radius ,h = height 

CALCULATION:

Here, we have radius = height  and volume = 64 \(\pi\) 

Volume = \(\pi\)r2h 

⇒ 64000 \(\pi\)= \(\pi\) r2× r       [1litre = 1000 cm3]

⇒ 64000  =  r3

⇒ r = 40 cm 

Hence, radius of the cylinder is 40 cm .

questions.question: The length of a hall is 21 m and the width is 14 m. The sum of the areas of the floor and the flat roof is equal to the sum of the areas of the four walls. Find the height of the hall.
questions.questionHtml: The length of a hall is 21 m and the width is 14 m. The sum of the areas of the floor and the flat roof is equal to the sum of the areas of the four walls. Find the height of the hall.
questions.solution:
Let the height of the hall be H

Area of floor = 21 × 14 = 294 m2

Sum of floor and ceiling = 588 m2

Area of four walls = 2 × (21 + 14) × H = 70H

70H = 588

H = 588/70 = 8.4 m

questions.question: A solid cube of side 8 cm is dropped into a rectangular container of length 16 cm, breadth 8 cm and height 15 cm which is partly filled with water. If the cube is completely submerged, then the rise of water level (in cm) is:
questions.questionHtml: A solid cube of side 8 cm is dropped into a rectangular container of length 16 cm, breadth 8 cm and height 15 cm which is partly filled with water. If the cube is completely submerged, then the rise of water level (in cm) is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Each side of the cube = 8 cm

The rectangular container has a length of 16 cm, breadth of 8 cm, and height of 15 cm

Formula used:

The volume of cube = (Edge)3

The volume of a cuboid = Length × Breadth × Height

Calculation:

The volume of cube = The volume of the rectangular container with a length of 16 cm, breadth of 8 cm, and height of the water level rise

Let, the height of the water level will rise = x cm

So, 83 = 16 × 8 × x

⇒ 512 = 128 × x

⇒ x = 512/128 = 4

∴ The rise of water level (in cm) is 4 cm

⇒ [(3.375/8) + 1 + (D3/2)3 ] = 3.375 ⇒ (D3/2)3 = 2.375 - (3.375/8) ⇒ D3 = 3√15.625 = 2.5

questions.question: A cylinder has some water in it at a height of 16 cm. If a sphere of radius 9 cm is put into it, then find the rise in the height of the water if the radius of the cylinder is 12 cm.
questions.questionHtml: A cylinder has some water in it at a height of 16 cm. If a sphere of radius 9 cm is put into it, then find the rise in the height of the water if the radius of the cylinder is 12 cm.
questions.solution:
Volume of water displaced by the sphere = \(\frac{4}{3}π (9)^3 \) = 972π cm3

Rise in height of the water level would be equal to the volume of the sphere.

We have,  \( π (12)^2h'\) = 972π 

⇒ h' = \( \frac{972}{144}\) = 6.75 cm
